title: Choosing depth without touching the test set
summary: Train, cross-validation, and a test set that is scored once.

choices.text: Use leave-one-out (k = n) on the non-test rows: every extra fold makes the estimate strictly better, and on 10,000 rows the extra fits cost nothing.
Hold out a test set first. Pick the depth with 5- or 10-fold cross-validation on the other rows, refit on all of them, and score the test set once.
Cross-validate on every row, including the rows you will publish as the test score, pick the depth that wins, and report that same cross-validation score.
Pick the depth on the test set, then report k-fold error on the other rows, since the test rows never touched training and k-fold averages over more data.
